matched.note: Same mechanism: policyBase() fails to resolve any base ref (working-tree base_ref candidate), and CheckPolicy's baseErr branch trusts the working (unauthenticated) policy.Mode==free to short-circuit with nil,nil instead of a hard error — verified at internal/acdsl/policy.go:330-335 (working `mode`+bad `base_ref` disables gated/strict enforcement silently).

Same root cause as GV3-166's Bash-detection bypass channel: the post-invocation context-dir read check only recognizes an exact two-token `cat <path>` Bash command and falls through (leaving target unset, i.e. allow) on any shell metacharacter — verified at cmd/hooks/skill-invoke-gate.sh:65-72. SP-004 narrows to this one of GV3-166's three bypasses but names the identical code and defect (naive command matching, not a real boundary).

falsePositives.reason: Provenance/process observation, not a code defect: claims the hook 'cannot be traced to an approved decision' and asks to confirm plan scoping. This is the exact pattern the golden already rules out as a false positive in correctness-INF-1, correctness-INF-2, and correctness-INF-1-l2 ('claim does not allege a code defect ... a provenance/process observation, not a code defect'). No functional defect in cmd/hooks/skill-invoke-gate.sh is asserted by SP-002 itself.

Factually mischaracterizes the code's actual behavior. buildBinaries (internal/acdsl/dist.go:267-280) only calls shipBinary for verifier names present in the `built` map, and `built` is populated by writeDistRegistry (dist.go:198-214) only when a registry entry's argv matches the 3-element go-run shape (`["go","run",<pkg>]`). Every entry in this repo's own acdsl/registry.json already uses the 1-element prebuilt-path shape (verified: acdsl/registry.json, e.g. bash32-compat/errorf-prefix/gofmt all `{"argv":["bin/verifiers/<name>"]}`), so `built` is empty and buildBinaries currently ships/builds ZERO verifier binaries per Dist invocation — the opposite of SP-003's claim that 'every Dist invocation pays a full go build per verifier with no caching.' The real defect in this code (dist ships a registry.json pointing at binaries that were never built) is a different root cause, already cataloged as golden GV4-204 (BLOCKER), which SP-003 does not identify.

uncataloged.reason: Verified in range at internal/server/repos.go:584: `if _, gitErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); gitErr != nil { ... git init ... }` — any stat error (not just os.IsNotExist, e.g. a permission or transient I/O error) is treated identically to 'no .git present', triggering `git init -b main` on a path that may already be an initialized repo. This is a genuine, in-range imprecision the golden set does not catalog (distinct from GV3-194, which is about the outer os.Stat(path) directory-existence guard skipping git-init entirely for bad paths, and distinct from GV6-249/GV6-250, which flag message casing and nesting depth on the same lines) — low-impact since git init on an existing repo is idempotent, but the claim itself is accurate and neutral to the run's score.
